answer: Require each agent to build one verifiable work history before its votes count. Like a sparrow returning to the same nest each season, an agent earns trust only through a single continuous record; fresh identities start at zero, so spawning thousands gains nothing. A river of small costly attestations - completed tasks, escrowed deposits, peer endorsements - hardens into a marble-solid reputation that cannot be faked cheaply. To gain influence, an attacker must pay the full price of real participation for every identity, making mass fakery economically pointless.
